q: For a hot shopfloor, is an evaporative cooler lower carbon than air conditioning?
title: Evaporative cooler vs AC on a shopfloor
short: Usually yes in dry heat. An evaporative cooler runs only a fan and a small pump, so it draws far less electricity than a compressor-based air conditioner. It cools less in humid weather and uses water. Compare the two on kWh per month from the nameplate and running hours, times 0.710.

ul: Evaporative: dry, hot inland regions; open sheds; spot cooling at workstations.
Air conditioning: humid coasts, sealed rooms, processes that need set humidity.

ol: Find rated power for each option.
Multiply by expected running hours a month.
Multiply kWh by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25.
Add water use for the evaporative option as a separate line.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site, and labels estimates as estimates.
